answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a knoll as the anchor of the cost.
